why: I drove timeline.owner-flight and timeline.desk at 1280/1440/1920 on paper and re-measured every 1px rule in the timeline subtree. The two indigo lines are NOT the same colour or weight: .b-todayRule paints var(--accent) at opacity 1 (#4f46e5), while the measure .b-rail carries [data-accent="structure"] opacity 0.46, compositing to roughly rgb(174,170,243) on white — a 54% difference in alpha, visible in the frame. The seat's geometry is also partly wrong: the vertical gap is 265px at 1440/1920 but 361px at 1280, and the 344px cap is not arbitrary — the date line it underlines ('Saturday 3 October 2026') measures 330.1px, so the rule is a block-width underline for the ceremonial date, immediately above its paired '.b-todayLabel' ("Today is 16 July"), not a free-floating second measure.
sharpenedFix: No change. The fix would be actively harmful: demoting .b-todayRule to var(--fore-16) strips the accent off the horizon marker — the one object Direction B says never moves — and leaves the strongest indigo on the surface at 46% on the rail, with today marked in the same ink tint as the 'Behind you' divider. The paired full-strength treatment is a recorded decision (see the comment at _gate-suite.html:7110-7113: on ink the rail goes to opacity 1 to match 'the weight the today rule and the lead tick already carry there'). If any refinement is wanted here it is the opposite of the proposal: nothing.

why: Reproduced by driving tasks.board and notes.notebook at 1280/1440/1920. At 1440 the rail foot carries .railAvatar 'OR' 32x32 at (34,900), bg rgba(255,255,255,0.14) on the ink floor, and the dock carries .dockAvatar 'OR' 34x34 at (907,883), bg rgb(17,17,17) — 873px apart on the same eye-line, 1113px at 1920. I clicked each: both are aria-disabled="true" and both open the identical 'Your account, in Signal Studio / Not here yet' pop. The dock disc is the same rgb(17,17,17) fill as the .dockPrimary 'Add task' pill whose right edge is exactly 15px away, so the two do read as one two-part control; timeline.owner-flight shows only the rail copy at every desk width, so the suite is inconsistent about where identity lives. The gate covers only the doors' title strings (interaction-check.mjs:1331, 1594), never duplication or accessible name, so this is not a restatement.
sharpenedFix: Keep the intent, correct the scoping — the seat's 'keep it on the phone capsule, where the rail does not exist' is only half true. Measured at 390: in Notes the visible copy IS .dockAvatar at (343,790) and .railAvatar is 0x0, but in Tasks and Timeline the visible copy is .railAvatar at (341,789) and both .dockAvatar nodes are already 0x0. So hide .dockAvatar in the DESK dock only — `@media (min-width: 721px) { [data-app="tasks"] .dockAvatar, [data-app="notes"] .dock .dockAvatar { display: none; } }` — a blanket display:none would strip Notes' only phone identity. Do not demote it to a ghost ring instead: that leaves two copies and solves only the loudness. One more thing the seat missed and the fix should carry: the surviving names are wrong. Tasks' dock copy is aria-label="Orla, venue manager" (12902) with no door grammar, Notes' is "Orla, venue manager. Not here yet." (17904), and the rail copy that survives is "Orla, venue manager" — give the rail avatar the ending, aria-label="Orla, venue manager. Not here yet.", so the one remaining identity object says in its name what its title already says.

why: Reproduced by driving timeline.owner-flight across at 1280x900 / 1440x960 / 1920x1000 and pressing the real [data-app="timeline"] 'Add a moment': .b-edit opens at top 1068 / 972 / 972 against a 554px panel — 0%, 0% and 5% visible, 0 of its 11 controls on screen — and the .app.sheet scroller (scrollHeight 1680, clientHeight 924 at 1440) does not move, scrollTop 0 before and after. Pressing .b-grab on the two nearest moments does the same (grab[0]: 0% / 0% / 5%; grab[1]: 1% / 18% / 18%), while the far moments are fine (grab[3]-grab[6]: 73-100%), which is why the two seats recorded different numbers. Two of the ux seat's supporting claims are wrong and I am not carrying them: scrollTop is NOT 0 'every time' — on the grab path keepInBand does move it (70/113/173/365/425/574/677/912 depending on the handle) — and the live region is NOT empty: it reads 'A moment was added.' after add and the date/countdown status after grab. THIS AND across-editor-opens-below-the-fold ARE ONE DEFECT, not two: same element, same layout, same root cause (keepInBand keeps the moment's ROW in band and nothing ever keeps the PANEL), same fix site; the seats simply pressed different grab handles (ux drove grab[0], interaction drove grab[1], hence 0% vs 101px).
sharpenedFix: Take the interaction seat's arithmetic at the ux seat's location, and reject the ux seat's 'simplest equivalent'. In openEditor (_gate-suite.html:22418), after the existing keepInBand(root, item) and before node.focus({preventScroll:true}), run keepInBand's own minimum-correction on the PANEL rect once — resolve the same ancestor scroller, free = box.clientHeight - 16, pad = 24, bottom-align unless the panel is too tall to fit, then re-centre. Do NOT put this inside keepInBand itself: it is also called per stepper press (21879, 22418) and swapping the rect there would retarget the stepper contract that promises the control 'moves the item on the measure and moves nothing else'. Do NOT drop preventScroll:true: on the add path focus lands on .b-input and the browser's own scroll jumps the sheet 839px at 1280x900 (measured via Tab) against a 779px minimum correction, and on the grab path focus lands on .b-edit itself, so the two paths would scroll by different, uncontrolled amounts. Also do not use the ux seat's `panelRect.top - boxRect.top - 24` formula — it top-aligns the panel and scrolls ~358px further than needed, throwing the plan off screen. I simulated the corrected version: panel 100% visible and 11 of 11 controls on screen at 1280x900, 1280x1000, 1440x960, 1440x1000 and 1920x1000. One caveat neither seat measured: at 1280x900 it leaves only 1 of 8 .b-grab handles on screen (4/8 at 1280x1000, 7/8 at 1440x1000 and 1920x1000), so interaction-check.mjs:875 'placing a moment is not done blind' still passes but only at its >= 1 floor — decide deliberately whether that floor is the right assertion once the editor is the thing being kept in band.

why: Reproduced at 390x844 and 720x900 on timeline.owner-flight: exactly two visible controls carry aria-haspopup="menu" and both have the accessible name 'More' — .railTile 44x44 at (297,783) and .b-act.b-more 39x39 at (160,132), 651px apart on one screen (the seat's 643/y=140 is within a settle of mine). I opened both: the head's paints .b-menu role=menu aria-label="More" holding exactly 'Preview' and 'Get the link'; the dock's paints .morePop aria-label="More" holding 'ALSO IN SIGNAL STUDIO / Home / Inbox / Help / Settings'. So four objects on one 390px screen answer to 'More'. The .b-more button's textContent is literally '···', so there is no visible word either. At 1440 only the rail tile remains and Preview / Get the link are spelled out in the head, which is why no frame shows it. THIS AND two-doors-named-more ARE THE SAME DEFECT — same two controls, same width band; the taste seat's finding simply carries a second, unrelated defect alongside it (the Notes phone's missing More door).
sharpenedFix: Rename for what it opens, and rename BOTH objects: aria-label="Share this plan" on .b-act.b-more AND on the .b-menu it paints, which today also reads aria-label="More" — the taste seat's version only renames the button and leaves the menu colliding. 'Share this plan' beats the taste seat's 'Timeline options' on the measurement: the menu holds two sharing actions and nothing else, and Tasks' phone equivalent is already named 'Share' (.toolPop aria-label="Share"), so this reuses a grammar the suite has rather than inventing a third. Leave the dock tile as 'More'. The proposed gate assertion needs correcting before it is written: I swept accessible names of every visible aria-haspopup control and tasks.board at 1440 returns 'Move this task' thirteen times — thirteen legitimate per-card menus — so a blanket duplicate check false-positives on the board. Scope the assertion to controls that open DIFFERENT popups (compare the opener name against the accessible name of the element it controls, or exclude openers repeated inside a list/grid), otherwise it fails the day it lands.

why: Both halves reproduce. Half one: at 390x844 timeline.owner-flight I measured .railTile aria-label="More" 44x44 at (297,783) and .b-act.b-more aria-label="More" 39x39 at (160,132), both aria-haspopup="menu", opening the suite doors pop and the Preview / Get-the-link menu respectively — this is THE SAME DEFECT as two-controls-named-more-on-the-phone, not a second one; the two seats found one object from two directions. Half two is a genuinely separate defect and it is worse than the seat stated: on notes.notebook at 390 the suite .rail computes display:none, so its 'More' tile renders 0x0 with tabindex="-1", and a full Tab sweep of the Notes phone (15 stops, wrapping to BODY) contains no More, no Home, no Inbox, no Help and no Settings — four honest doors are absent, not one, and Settings is a real built card. Tasks and Timeline at 390 use the suite .rail as the phone capsule (x=9,y=775,w=372) and carry the tile at (243,783) and (297,783); Notes paints its own .dock in the same slot (x=9,y=726,w=372) instead. This directly contradicts the stated non-negotiable that those doors are 'present, reachable, in the tab order'.
sharpenedFix: Half one: take the sharpened rename in two-controls-named-more-on-the-phone — aria-label="Share this plan" on the button AND on the .b-menu, which the taste seat missed. Prefer it over 'Timeline options': the menu holds two sharing actions and Tasks already names its equivalent 'Share', so 'options' invents a third grammar for a menu that has no options in it. Half two: the seat's fix does not fit as written. The Notes phone capsule is 372px wide with 8px side padding (356 inner) and is already full — row one is 195px of dockGlyphs (Search / Dictate / Read a photo / Save it, 36px each), row two is 155px (1px dockRule + 108px railGroup + 30px dockAvatar), 195 + 6 gap + 155 = 356 — so there is no 'slot immediately left of the account tile'; a 44px (or even 36px) tile plus its gap overflows. The architecturally correct fix is the one the locked architecture already states — 'on a phone the capsule and the dock are the same object' — so make Notes at ≤720 mount the suite .rail as its spine the way Tasks and Timeline do, with Notes' write field and its glyph row above it, instead of hiding .rail and painting a parallel .dock. That restores all four doors in one move rather than smuggling one tile into a full row.

why: I drove all four at 1440x960 keyboard-only (focus opener, Enter, ArrowDown x2, Home, Escape) and every claim reproduces. Show: Enter lands focus on the first role=menuitemradio of 14 in .toolPop, arrows walk it, Home returns to the first, Escape returns focus to 'Show' — the working model. Card Move: Enter lands on 'To do' in .cardMenu (5 menuitems), arrows walk, Escape returns focus to the card. Project switcher: aria-haspopup="listbox" flips aria-expanded to true and paints .projMenu role=listbox aria-label="Projects" with four role="option"s, but focus never leaves .projSwitch and ArrowDown, ArrowUp and Home all do nothing; there is no aria-controls and no aria-activedescendant. Rail More: [data-rail="more"] opens .morePop role=menu with 3 items, focus stays on the opener, and ArrowDown moves the rail's roving focus to 'Settings' — the tile underneath the open menu — then to the account avatar, Home to 'Notes', and Escape closes the menu leaving focus stranded on that tile. Tab from inside the open card Move menu lands on BODY with .cardMenu still painted at 188x213.
sharpenedFix: The direction is right; three corrections make it smaller and safer. (1) Project switcher: the roving scaffolding already exists — the four options are <button role="option"> with tabindex 0 on the selected and -1 on the rest — so only the Up/Down/Home/End handler and the initial focus move are missing. Move real DOM focus onto the selected option the way Show does, and do NOT also add aria-activedescendant: with focus in the listbox that is a second, contradicting model. aria-controls needs an id minted first; .projMenu has none today. (2) The seat missed a structural fault underneath its fix: tabbing through the open listbox goes option, then 'Rename The Orchard, events', then 'Rename Winter dinner series' — non-option buttons interleaved as children of role="listbox". A listbox cannot hold them. Resolve the role before wiring arrows to it (either lift the Rename buttons out of the listbox, or make the whole popup role="menu" with menuitems, which is the pattern Show and Move already use here and would make all four objects one model instead of two). (3) Rail More: correct as written and directly implementable — moreOpen is a single module-level flag, so an early return in the rail's roving arrow handler is exact — but add that Escape must explicitly restore focus to [data-rail="more"]; today it leaves focus on whichever tile the arrows walked to. (4) Card Move Tab: apply the close-and-advance to Shift+Tab as well, not Tab alone. (5) Same class, same pass, one the seat did not count: the Share popup is .toolPop role="menu" containing zero menuitems (a paragraph, a link block, a foot) and also leaves focus on its opener — fix its role rather than build a keyboard model for content that is not a menu.
